Insurance Eligibility & Benefits Verification

Confirmed Before the Visit, Not Discovered After the Denial

Eligibility verification confirms a patient's insurance is active, what it actually covers, and what the patient will owe, before a single service is delivered. It sounds like a small administrative step, but a large share of claim denials trace back to exactly this: coverage that lapsed, a plan that changed, or a service that needed authorization no one checked for.

Skipping this step doesn't remove the problem, it just moves the discovery from the front desk to a denied claim weeks later, after the service has already been delivered and the cost already incurred. By then, the only option is an appeal, a write-off, or a surprise bill to the patient.

PMEX checks coverage, benefits, deductibles and authorization requirements before every scheduled visit, so the front desk, the provider and the patient all know exactly where things stand before care is delivered.

What Gets Checked

  • ✓Active coverage status on the date of service
  • ✓Covered services and treatment limitations
  • ✓Deductibles, copays and coinsurance amounts
  • ✓Referral and authorization requirements
  • ✓Primary and secondary insurance coordination
  • ✓Patient responsibility estimates before service
  • ✓Coverage exclusions specific to the plan
  • ✓Pre-service documentation of verification results

The Verification Process

Four Checks, Completed Before the Appointment

1

Collect Details

Name, date of birth, insurance provider and policy number gathered at scheduling.

2

Verify Coverage

Policy status, covered services and limitations confirmed directly with the payer.

3

Confirm Costs

Deductibles, copays and coinsurance calculated into a patient-ready estimate.

4

Document & Flag

Results recorded, with authorization needs flagged before the visit happens.
